text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. An API allows your program to communicate with another service by sending HTTP requests, such as GET or POST, to a specific URL. Most APIs return data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Before you can access protected resources, you usually need authentication, often through an API key or token. It is also important to respect rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make within a certain time. Finally, good error handling helps your application respond gracefully when something goes wrong, such as a network failure or an invalid request.
